newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bankers Trust cuts Mexico GDP forecast to 4.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust cuts Mexico GDP forecast to 4.5 pct.

text.p: Bankers Trust Research said on Monday it had cut its 1997 GDP growth forecast for Mexico to 4.5 percent from 4.8 percent, adding the biggest threat to growth was sluggish consumer demand.

"We have reduced our forecast for GDP growth from 4.8 percent to 4.5 percent year on year and the risk may be to the downside," Denis Parisien, vice president for Latin American Research said in a report to investors.
Bankers Trust Research is the research department for BT Securities Corp.

"The biggest threat to growth is the lack of comsumer demand," he added. "The main impediment to the recovery in consumption is that real wage growth remains in negative territory and employment growth, while strong in the manufacturing sector, remains fairly weak overall."
Earlier on Monday Mexico released first quarter GDP growth of 5.1 percent, which was in line with revised forecasts after the government deflated higher expectations late last week.

"Mexican Q1 industry and trade data have thus far shown that the large year on year percent gains reminiscent of the economic recovery in 1996 are receding, as the base period for 1997 comparision rises and the lack of dynamism in private consumption remains a serious drag on growth," Parisien added.
He also pointed to a slowdown in industrial production and in trade. "As a result we are lowering our forecast moderately for Mexican GDP growth from 4.8 percent to 4.5 percent," he said.
